thread:
incident-bot: Paging SRE on-call — elevated 5xx and tail latency in EU region for inference endpoints. Trigger: latency SLO breach + error spike across multiple routes. Initial signal at 00:18 UTC; error rate ~20% for tier=free, ~8% for tier=standard.

Sam: grabbing. tagging @Maria and @Jordan. any obvious deploys?

Maria: no deploys in last 30m. pulling top callers and route heatmap now.

Jordan: KV cache churn on model-x-16k looks high, lots of prefix misses. suspicion: long-context demo traffic + aggressive sampling.

Sam: quick mitigation idea: emergency steer for low-priority traffic (free tier) -> 1) hard rate cap 2) steer to batch-friendly, lower-memory model variant 3) disable streaming for that cohort to reduce open connections 4) notify CS. Will try minimal changes first.

ops-runbook-bot: Runbook -> https://redwood.internal/runbooks/eu-latency-spike (steps: rate-limit, steer, monitor 5m windows, CS notify).

Maria: pulling top org IDs — corp-analytics (org-112), demo-app (org-287), search-proxy (org-330). Most traffic from corp-analytics looks like single-token heavy loops.

Sam: applying emergency policy via routing CLI, staging tested. command I used:

```
redwood routing update-policy --policy emergency-eu-tilt \
  --match "region=eu,tier=free" \
  --actions "rate_limit=20r/s,route=model-small-quant,disable_stream=true"
```

Jordan: recommend also reduce global burst tokens for free tier to avoid sudden spikes spilling into other regions.

Maria: pushing the policy to prod now. console change at 00:26 UTC.

deploy-bot: emergency-eu-tilt policy deployed to prod by Maria (web-console). :white_check_mark:

Sam: policy in. initial effect: free-tier 5xx rate dropped 20% -> ~7% within 3 minutes. p95 latency improved ~220ms -> ~90ms for routed requests.

CS Pager: notified CS leads and sent targeted messages to affected customers (org-112, org-287, org-330). Provided mitigation steps: reduce concurrency, add jitter to retries.

Sam: hands-off to Lee for the next shift — handing off current state and actions taken. key checks: watch for spillover to us-west, verify no backlog on model-small-quant, monitor streaming connections.

Lee: acknowledged. I'll keep the emergency policy and increase sampling on traces for the next 30m. If error rate for standard tier rises >5%, escalate back to Sam.

Priya: suggestion: add region pin fallback for EU -> prefer eu-west primary, fallback to eu-south only if node pool healthy. prevents cross-region routing that added latency earlier.

Jordan: adding global token reduction for free tier from 200->50 and reducing per-org burst from 50->10. applying now:

```
# quota adjustments
redwood quota update --scope tier:free --burst 50 --global-burst 50
redwood quota update --org org-112 --burst 10
```

Maria: applied quotas. monitoring.

Sam: results after 20m: free-tier 5xx at 4.2%, standard at 1.1%. overall p95 across EU routes stable under SLO. CS updated customers with ETA for full recovery.

CS Pager: customers responded: two smaller customers accepted workaround; corp-analytics wanted an SLA note — escalation to account team queued.

ops-runbook-bot: remind: if we see increased errors after relaxing limits, rollback policy with `redwood routing rollback emergency-eu-tilt` and revert quotas.

Sam: stepping out. leaving incident in monitoring mode. Lee, please ping if anything degrades.

Lee: will monitor. increasing alerting threshold to catch p95 regressions sooner.

deploy-bot: policy metrics: traffic diverted ~18% of EU requests to model-small-quant, connection count decreased 30%.

Jordan: follow-up action for infra: investigate KV cache eviction tuning and look at prefix caching TTLs for model-x-16k. I'll open a ticket.

Maria: prepping postmortem notes, including customer impact table and timeline.

incident-bot: After 2h the incident is stable. error rates remain <1% for all tiers, no further escalation. Sam closed incident at 02:35 UTC. :white_check_mark:
